learn.title: C does not check
learn.body: If `a` has 3 elements and you read `a[5]`, C does not stop you. No error appears at run time. The program just reads or writes whatever memory sits there. This is undefined behavior.

learn.title: The classic bug
learn.body: The loop uses `<=`, so the last pass reads `a[3]`, which does not exist. The first three prints are 1 2 3, then the output is unpredictable.

learn.title: Undefined means anything
learn.body: The program may print garbage, crash with a segmentation fault, or even look fine today and fail tomorrow. Writing past the end is worse: it can overwrite other variables. Never rely on what happens.

learn.title: Catch it with a tool
learn.body: Build with AddressSanitizer. The bug program then stops and reports `stack-buffer-overflow` and the line of the bad read.

learn.title: Check before you index
learn.body: When an index comes from outside, test it first. Here 5 is not between 0 and 2, so it prints `bad index`.

learn.title: Fix the bug
steps: Length is 3, so valid indexes are 0, 1, 2
The loop runs while `i <= 3`, which includes 3

learn.body: Most out-of-bounds bugs are `<=` where `<` was meant. Check every loop bound against the length.

questions.prompt: What does C do when you read `a[5]` of a 3-element array?
choices: Nothing special: the behavior is undefined
questions.explanation: C does not check bounds, so anything can happen.

questions.prompt: What kind of loop condition causes the classic bug?
choices: `i <= n` for an array of length `n`
questions.explanation: `i <= n` makes the last pass use index `n`, one past the end.

questions.prompt: In `int a[3]`, what is the first invalid index above 0? Type the number.
questions.explanation: Valid indexes are 0, 1 and 2, so 3 is the first one past the end.

questions.prompt: Reading or writing past the end of an array is \_\_ behavior.
questions.explanation: The language makes no promise about what happens.

questions.prompt: Which tool reports an out-of-bounds access while the program runs?
questions.explanation: Build with `-fsanitize=address` and it names the line.

questions.prompt: Which test protects `a[idx]` for an array of length 3?
questions.explanation: Both ends need checking. A negative index is out of bounds too.

questions.prompt: The program ran fine on your computer with an out-of-bounds read. What does that tell you?
choices: Nothing, it can still fail elsewhere
questions.explanation: Undefined behavior can look correct by luck.

questions.prompt: Match each situation to what you should expect.
questions.explanation: Only indexes 0 up to length minus 1 are safe.
